lines.en: Two blocks tall, with steady steps.
My bracers are heavy.
The savanna grass bends as I pass.
I walk on hoof-like feet.
I carry a tool kit on my back.
Step by step, like keeping time.
I scan around, alert.
I'm a rabbit that knows how to punch.
I patrol near my anchor.
I can be put to logging.
My ears never stop listening.
One bound clears the shrubs.
I stand with bracers raised.

lines.zh: 一百到两百五十点生命
lines.en: A hundred to two hundred fifty points.
I've trained my fists a long while.
This hide is tough.
I wait for my master's order.
Grass sways at my feet.
My knuckles crack twice.
I can fell trees, or fight.
Footsteps on the wind, getting closer.
My ears are very flexible.
It's still early; I have time for a few rounds.
I haven't met a worthy opponent.
I know this savanna.
My bracer came loose, so I strap it tight again.
Your stance isn't good.
My strikes land heavy.
Care to try my fists?
I can hear what you intend.
Standing before me is bold.
I'm no wild rabbit.
I have a master.
If you don't strike, neither do I.
These bracers stop blades.
You're carrying an axe.
I know logging well.
Don't wave that in front of me.
My fists hit harder than they look.
You'd better back up two steps.
That frame of yours won't take one punch.
Standing closer wouldn't matter.
Half a step back; stance holds.
Thick hide, thick skin — come again.
The bracer took most of it.
I clench my teeth and make no sound.
My hide is thicker than it looks.
That last punch was only seven tenths.
I keep this debt scratched on my bracer.
I straighten up again.
My legs hold steady and my fists aren't soft yet.
Plant your feet — let's go again.
Feed? I'm not picky.
Set it down; I'll eat slowly.
At my size, a little isn't enough.
I can still work after eating.
I don't drop my bracers to eat.
Keep it back; I don't want it soiled.
I'll remember this meal.
My table manners aren't pretty.
More, and I'll work till dark.
Don't hold it up; I can reach.
I eat fast, and stop fast.
Is there anything else to eat?
You hit my bracer.
My feet might as well be nailed.
You hit my bracer and fall back half a step.
This body is heavy.
A bump won't stop my punch.
I turn aside.
My ear got bumped.
That force is nothing.

lines.zh: 你的靴底压在我脚趾上
lines.en: Your boot sole is pressing on my toes.

lines.zh: 再挤一次，我的拳就到了
lines.en: Shove once more and my fist arrives.
First I see if you can fight.
This body is built for work.

lines.zh: 这些事我只会用拳头讲
lines.en: I only know how to say these things with my fists.
These things take time.
My bracers aren't for giving.
Train your fists first.
There's much to do on the savanna.
You're standing too near.
I still have wood to cut.
Don't hold up my work.
A piece of wood on the ground.
I lift it one-handed.
I lift this log with one hand.
I tuck it under my arm.
I can find what falls in the grass.
This one could be a handle.
I'll take it back to use.
Don't grab; this is mine.
I pick it up and inspect it.
I don't need a crate.
My stance is set.
The bracers guard my front.
If you want a fight, come on.
This punch will be heavy.
My ears track you.
You're backing off faster than I expected.
I'm not the type to start trouble.
But you crossed my line.
I call out before I strike.
Before I raise my fist, one question.
Three hundred points; a long fight.

lines.zh: 这双护腕，就是我的兵器
lines.en: These two bracers are all the weapon I need.
I hug the ground and creep in inch by inch.
The bracers stay in front.
The moment your hand moves, I know.

lines.zh: 你抬手的动作我看过了
lines.en: I've seen your tell.
I needn't be fast; I'm heavy enough.
No cover on this savanna.
Your steps have gone sloppy.

lines.zh: 你吸气的时候，我就进半步
lines.en: When you breathe in, I close half a step.
Your flesh shows through the seams of your armor.
I can tell you're afraid.
Two more steps.
My fists are clenched; I wait for you to move first.
A straight punch.
My bracer sweeps across.
I drive upward from below.
This fist hits your armor.
One punch sends you back two steps.
I close the gap again.
My knee drives in.
No tricks; only force.

lines.zh: 挡得一拳挡不住第二拳
lines.en: Block one, not the second.
I switch hands and strike.
Your hand's numb, isn't it?
Fists back, stance straight.
I step out of the light.
My bracers land first.
The savanna has one more rabbit.
I stand straight, two blocks tall.
I listen to my surroundings.
There's work here.
I set my tool kit down.
I clench a fist to test it.
The wind carries wood smell.
I step in at an easy pace.
My ears told me you were coming.
This is room enough to plant my feet.
Fur singed; I patted it out.
I fell and my leg jarred.
I can't fight the water.
The blast left my ears ringing.
An arrow caught in my bracer.
This force isn't from fists.
Hungry, I can't chop wood.
Lightning struck my bracer.
The savanna vanished below.
